title: A Quadratic in sin x: 2sin^2 x - 3sin x + 1 = 0
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Solve the trigonometric equation 2 sin^2 x - 3 sin x + 1 = 0 for all real x by treating it as a quadratic in u = sin x and respecting the range restriction of the sine function.

steps.title: Substitute u = sin x
steps.explanation: Every appearance of sin x can be renamed u, converting the transcendental equation into an ordinary quadratic with the side constraint that u must lie in the sine range.
steps.why: The structure 2(sin x)^2 - 3(sin x) + 1 is polynomial in the single quantity sin x, so the substitution is lossless on [-1, 1].

steps.title: Factor the Quadratic
steps.explanation: The middle term splits as -2u - u, giving the factorization (2u - 1)(u - 1); both candidate values happen to be admissible sine outputs.
steps.why: A product vanishes only when a factor vanishes (zero-product property), and both roots pass the range test |u| <= 1.

steps.title: Solve sin x = 1/2
steps.explanation: Within one period the reference angle with sine 1/2 is pi/6, and by symmetry the second solution on [0, 2pi) is its supplement 5pi/6; adding full turns generates all solutions.
steps.why: Sine is positive in quadrants I and II and has fundamental period 2*pi, so the two branches plus 2*k*pi exhaust the solution set.

steps.title: Solve sin x = 1
steps.explanation: The sine reaches its maximum 1 at exactly one point per period, the peak at pi/2, so this branch contributes a single congruence class rather than a pair.
steps.why: The unit-circle height equals 1 only at the topmost point; periodicity then replicates that peak every 2*pi.
